steps: Metabolism is the sum of all the chemical reactions taking place in the body of an organism.
Catabolism is the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler molecules, releasing energy.
Anabolism is the synthesis of complex molecules from simpler molecules, requiring energy.
items.finalAnswer: Metabolism includes all chemical reactions in an organism; catabolism breaks molecules down and releases energy, while anabolism builds molecules and requires energy.

steps: Anabolism demands an input of energy.
For example, the synthesis of proteins from amino acids is an anabolic reaction.
items.finalAnswer: Anabolism requires energy; for example, the synthesis of proteins from amino acids.

steps: An enzyme is a biological catalyst, usually a protein, that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up in the reaction.
Enzymes regulate and speed up the metabolic reactions in living organisms.
items.finalAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up metabolic reactions without being used up.

steps: The active site is the specific region of an enzyme where the substrate binds and the reaction takes place.
The shape of the active site is complementary to a particular substrate.
This makes an enzyme specific: it acts only on its particular substrate.
items.finalAnswer: The active site binds a particular substrate, giving the enzyme its specificity.

steps: As substrate concentration increases, the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction increases.
The rate reaches a maximum when all the enzyme active sites are occupied.
After this point, adding more substrate does not increase the reaction rate.
items.finalAnswer: Increasing substrate concentration increases enzyme activity until all active sites are occupied; then the rate remains constant.

steps: Pepsin works best in an acidic medium, at about pH 2.
Trypsin works best in an alkaline medium, at about pH 8.
items.finalAnswer: Pepsin has an optimum pH of about 2, while trypsin has an optimum pH of about 8.

steps: The optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
The optimum pH is the pH at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
items.finalAnswer: Optimum temperature and pH are the conditions at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
